responseText:
Good question — CSVs strip workbook structure and formulas, so it’s easy to lose or corrupt numbers if you don’t prepare. Short checklist and safe workflow to follow before you paste/export:

1. Back up the workbook first
   - Save a copy of the original workbook (so you don’t lose formulas or sheet links).

2. Understand what the portal needs
   - Confirm required columns, order, date formats, delimiter (comma vs semicolon), and encoding (usually UTF‑8).
   - Confirm whether the portal expects numeric values (no currency symbols) and how it expects dates (ISO yyyy-mm-dd is safest).

3. Replace formulas with values (don’t upload formulas)
   - CSV can’t keep formulas. Create a values-only copy of the sheet: select all → Copy → Paste Special → Values into a new sheet or a copy of the workbook.
   - This ensures the CSV contains the evaluated numbers rather than formula text.

4. Resolve cross-sheet references
   - Your SUMIFs that reference another sheet will evaluate to a number in the values-only copy — but only if the referenced sheet was available when you pasted values.
   - If those SUMIF results depend on live data on another sheet that won’t be present to the portal, ensure those referenced ranges are included (flatten them into the sheet) or recompute the final numbers before exporting.

5. Check for hidden/filtered rows, merged cells, and headers
   - Hidden rows/columns and filtered rows may still be included or excluded unexpectedly. Unhide and verify.
   - Merged cells often cause misaligned CSV columns — unmerge and place values into single cells.

6. Check numeric precision and rounding
   - CSV will capture the actual underlying value, not the displayed rounding. If you need rounded numbers, apply ROUND(...) or round in the values-only copy before exporting.
   - Verify totals after converting to values.

7. Look for error values and #REF / #N/A
   - Make sure no formula errors exist. They will become literal text in CSV and may break imports.

8. Remove or neutralize formula/CSV injection risk
   - Cells that begin with =, +, -, or @ can be interpreted as formulas by spreadsheet software and may be security flagged by some systems. If the portal treats raw CSVs in a spreadsheet, either ensure the portal sanitizes inputs or prefix such fields with an apostrophe (') or otherwise neutralize them if appropriate.

9. Remove formatting characters that break CSV parsing
   - Remove thousands separators (commas) if you’re using comma delimiters, or use a different delimiter if required.
   - Remove currency symbols if the portal expects plain numbers.
   - Ensure text fields don’t contain unescaped newlines or delimiter characters, or ensure they are properly quoted.

10. Verify data types
   - Dates should be exported as text in a stable format (yyyy-mm-dd).
   - Leading zeros (IDs) must be preserved: ensure they’re stored as text before export.

11. Check named ranges, tables, and dynamic ranges
   - Named ranges and Excel tables aren’t preserved in CSV. Flatten any dynamic ranges so the values you need are present.

12. Test by inspecting the raw CSV
   - Save or export as CSV and open it in a plain text editor to confirm columns, delimiters, encoding, and values look correct.
   - Do a quick test upload (or upload to a sandbox) with a small sample to confirm the portal accepts it.

13. Final sanity checks
   - Recompute grand totals and compare them to the original workbook totals.
   - Confirm there are no leftover formulas (cells beginning with "=") in the CSV if the portal doesn’t allow them.

Recommended safe workflow (quick):
- Save backup copy.
- Duplicate workbook or create a new temporary sheet.
- In the duplicate, Paste Special → Values for the budget tab (so everything is values).
- Unhide/unmerge and clean formatting, round numbers if needed.
- Save As → CSV (active sheet) or export the values into the portal’s CSV template.
- Open CSV in text editor, verify, then upload/test.

If you want, tell me:
- whether you’re saving from Excel or copying into a portal UI,
- which delimiter/locale the portal expects,
and I’ll give step-by-step commands for Excel/Google Sheets and a small checklist to run before upload.
